analysis:
This PR splits local authorization freshness into two paths in ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.swift.

- liveDecision (head 44-58) keeps the existing checks: process identity, coordinator match, finite timestamps, writtenAt within 10s, receivedAt >= startedAt, status==online and protocolVersion==1.
- currentStatus (head 10-22) re-adds the strict check now-receivedAt <= snapshotMaxAge. It behaves as before and is still returned by currentProviderAuthorization (head 106-117).
- displayedStatus (head 28-40) also accepts a decision received more than 10s ago if the App Attest lease is still unexpired.
- summary (head 68-100) gives positive removal advice only when removalAuthorization equals the displayed status and removalReady holds. A late lease therefore yields "needs fresh coordinator readiness; keep profiles."

DoctorRunner.swift (head 37-38, 78-79) takes both values from the same state and the same `now`.

Security relevance (TB-011, TB-002, T-053, T-057):
- The relaxed path only affects local operator display and the doctor pass/warn level. It also hides the AttestationReadiness and MDM hints (base 67, 108).
- The base header (line 3-4) and TB-002 state that doctor verdicts and local snapshots are not trust evidence. The coordinator re-checks at every handoff, so serving permission is unchanged.
- Residual effect: a delayed revocation may still display as authorized until expires_at. That is a cosmetic delay bounded by the coordinator-chosen lease, not a permission change.
- MDM removal guidance stays strict, so the TB-011 rule that removal needs a fresh decision is preserved.
- The docs addition (head 92-106) matches the code.

Integration questions (callers not in this batch):
1. Verify the `darkbloom status` caller passes currentProviderAuthorization, not the displayed value, as removalAuthorization.
2. Verify UnenrollCommand+KeepServing.swift still uses currentProviderAuthorization/currentStatus before and after profile inspection.
3. Check that any other callers of the old summary(_:now:) signature were updated.

No regression identified in the supplied units.
